expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: Rests on item 0: the 10-Q's company-level inventory/WIP build ($47.6m to $79.0m) plus 26-28 week lead times and 'no stairstep' commentary against a Q4 bar of only +3.5% q/q, on the guidance line that drove +76% in April. I re-filed item 8 (Broadcom: custom-chip clients stay on copper inside racks through 2028) as a finding rather than a drop: nothing in a primary document contradicts it, and the searcher used the same CEO's remarks as a bullish finding in item 1.

opus5.note: Rests on item 0 against item 1, and they genuinely fight. Item 0 is the CEO on the record eleven weeks into the quarter that the summer 'did not improve', on top of a July CFO statement that trends point to the low end of the FY volume guide, into a +15.7% 20-day run-up and a +5% no-news session the day of the print — a guide cut or narrowing is the line that cost 9.6% in April. Item 1's marketing-spend arithmetic off the company's own 8-K ($28.7m spent in H1 against a $0-20m FY guide) is real EPS support but EPS is not what this stock pays for, and the CFO's 'H2 spend still up YoY' contradicts the phasing. Item 4's 15.4% short, 5.1 days to cover, shrinks the negative as a squeeze mechanism rather than cancelling it.

opus55.note: Rests on item 0 (the CEO saying in September the summer did not improve, so the volume guide is at risk after a 15.7% unexplained run-up), offset by item 1's company-document marketing-spend arithmetic supporting EPS and a 15% short that cushions any negative.

sonnet55.note: Weak-volume guide risk (item 0) is offset by the H2 marketing-spend arithmetic (item 1) and a crowded 15% short, with a balanced skew and a run-up into the print.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0: the CEO said eleven weeks into Q3 that the summer 'did not improve' and the trend 'has not been good', which makes a volume-guide cut or narrowing (the line that cost -9.6% in April) likely under an interim CFO (item 3), while the stock has rallied 18% into the print; shrunk for the 15.4% crowded short and five-of-seven up history (item 4), and partly offset by the company-document arithmetic that H2 marketing spend must fall $9-29m YoY (item 1), which the CFO's own call comment undercuts.

opus5.note: A thin net positive, carried by item 4 (H1 EBITDA +4% above a +1-3% FY range, H2 capex guided to ~C$550m/q against C$964m in Q3'25, so Q3 FCF steps up hard) on the exact line that bought +11% intraday in Q1'26, plus item 2's three-carrier October price increases and item 8's depressed sector positioning; offset by item 1's very hard 62k postpaid comp. fable51.note: A balanced set that nets mildly positive: the company's own H1 numbers (EBITDA +4% above the FY +1-3% range, capex halving in H2 so Q3 FCF steps up, item 4), October's industry-wide $5 price hikes drowned out by the SpaceX sell-off (item 2) and a sector at multi-year lows with the Q1'26 +11% precedent off low expectations (item 8), against a very hard postpaid net-add comp (item 1); the hybrid refinance (item 13) is filed as a small financing cost rather than dropped as a duplicate, and the scale is the real print reactions (+11, -4, +5), not the baseline's monthly 6-K noise.

opus5.note: Close to a non-result with a slight negative tilt. Item 0's guide-raise arithmetic (H1 ex-energy +15.2% against a +10-11% FY guide, occupancy +200bp to 91.7%, and last year's Q3 raised the margin guide) is the only sizeable positive, but on four analysts the models almost certainly already sit above the guide and the +10% run-up to 2.6% below the 52-week high is what pricing that in looks like, so it is capped. Against it, item 5 is the kind of thing that pays here — Bajío stabilised occupancy 96.0% to 92.2% and North same-store 97.1% to 93.0%, in the Q2 filing tables and in none of the wire copy — but it has to be sized net of Monterrey, Mexico City and the new deliveries that carried the total. Item 4 is deliberately small because the run-up already discounted item 0 once. Item 6 (USMCA) left at a proxy's weight.
